blocks.content: Quiz: In SpeedBlip's GitHub-to-Netlify pipeline, what happens when a git push contains a TypeScript type error that breaks the build?
Tap an option below to answer:
Netlify deploys the broken code and shows a warning on the live site
Netlify does not deploy broken builds. If yarn build fails, the deploy stops and the previous working version stays live at the URL.
Netlify does not deploy broken builds. If yarn build fails, the deploy stops and the previous working version stays live at the URL.
GitHub automatically reverts the commit to the previous working state
GitHub does not automatically revert commits. The commit stays in the repository history, but Netlify's deploy gate prevents broken code from going live.
GitHub does not automatically revert commits. The commit stays in the repository history, but Netlify's deploy gate prevents broken code from going live.
The build fails in Netlify and the previous successful deploy stays live at the URL
Correct. Netlify runs yarn build on every push. If it fails - for any reason including TypeScript errors - the deploy is aborted and the previous passing deploy continues to serve the live URL.
Correct. Netlify runs yarn build on every push. If it fails - for any reason including TypeScript errors - the deploy is aborted and the previous passing deploy continues to serve the live URL.
The broken build deploys to a staging URL while the live URL stays clean
Netlify can be configured with branch previews, but by default, a failed build simply fails. There is no automatic staging URL for broken builds on the main branch.
Netlify can be configured with branch previews, but by default, a failed build simply fails. There is no automatic staging URL for broken builds on the main branch.
